claim: Repo claims items can be spawned as world pickups via a game-systems singleton (0x1426ffaa8, +0x6d28 world drop manager) and functions LootRecordInit/FromItem/Destroy and WorldDropSpawn(pose, lootRecord, id, worldCtx, flag), mirroring Combat.Action.InventoryItemDropLoot.
evidence: GameOffsets.h:115 kGameSystemsSingleton = 0x1426ffaa8ull; // +0x6d28 = world drop manager; :119 kWorldDropSpawn = 0x1407a10a0ull
game_build_compatibility: UNKNOWN: repo records no game version, Steam buildid, exe hash or build check; it only states a ~112 MB x64 Steam exe with SteamStub v3.1 + Denuvo (docs/reverse-engineering.md:12,21-29). Our exe is 117732784 bytes (~112.3 MiB), consistent but not proof of 1.0.8874.0 / build 3095001. Offsets are hardcoded file RVAs (no pattern scan, no version gate), so any mismatch with 1.0.8874.0 would silently hook wrong code.
limitations: Author notes direct inventory mutation caused hangs/crashes; only the world-drop route is used. Relevance to co-op is an example of spawning a world object via engine code, not actor spawning.
next_experiment: Statically locate the Combat.Action.InventoryItemDropLoot string in our exe and compare the handler RVA with the repo claim (0x140f14fa0).
